metadata.title: देश के सबसेअमीर राज्य के आदिवासी |  Life of Adivasi in Richest State of India - Maharashtra
metadata.description:
Maharashtra is often called India’s richest state, yet within it lies Nandurbar — the poorest district of the state. Hidden deep in the forests of the Satpura range, this region reflects a harsh and unequal reality of development.

More than 70% of Nandurbar’s population belongs to Adivasi (tribal) communities. Life here is closely tied to forests and natural resources, but it is also defined by daily hardship and risk.

In this ground report, @MainBhiBharat Editor Shyam Sunder travels into the Satpura jungles to understand tribal life from close quarters. Working alongside Adivasi women, he witnesses the exhausting and dangerous task of collecting water — walking long distances through difficult terrain, carrying heavy pots, and risking injury every single day just to meet a basic need.

This report brings attention to the invisible struggles of tribal women and raises urgent questions about inequality, access to water, and development in one of Maharashtra’s most neglected districts.
